description:
Return a queued owned-job receipt (data.job_id and data.status). Read the exact id through job_service.get_job for the complete former response in job.result or the typed failure in job.error. Admission retains payload references locally; uncertain effects require reconciliation and must never be replayed automatically.

Hard-delete a specific set of memories by id, with their embeddings.

Use cases:
- Knowledge base lifecycle management (remove specific ingested chunks by id, e.g. a per-file re-index or a targeted sweep, without a tag round-trip).
- Precise cleanup when the caller already holds the exact memory ids to remove.

The id-list counterpart of delete_memories_by_tag. Cascade vector-first: the embeddings are deleted before the memory records, so an interrupted delete leaves at most an orphan memory (reconcilable via reindex), never an orphan embedding. This is destructive and irreversible.
embedding_description: Delete a specific list of memories by id (destructive), removing their vector embeddings too. The id counterpart of delete_memories_by_tag — use when you already hold the exact memory ids, e.g. knowledge-base per-file re-index or a targeted chunk sweep, rather than deleting by tag.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: The complete memory-operation response from the exact admitted job; the immediate response is a queued job receipt.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: The specified memories were hard-deleted along with their embeddings. If these ids backed a knowledge-base corpus, the corresponding content is no longer retrievable; re-ingest if it should return.

error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: DatabaseError: failed to delete memory records. VectorStoreError: failed to delete associated embeddings.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For database errors: verify state storage is accessible. For vector store errors: verify vector storage is accessible.
